errorCodes.meaning: The named host could not be resolved, advertises no transport this recipient speaks, or did not answer the registration. Reports the registration only, never the delivery of the room's revocation list, which is reported in a successful response's `revocation`.

The host answered and declined the registration — commonly its own creation policy. Its reason is carried in `details`. Reports the registration only, never the delivery of the room's revocation list, which is reported in a successful response's `revocation`.

DigestMultibase.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.
DigestMultibase.title: DigestMultibase

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

RecordRetention.description:
How long a room keeps its records, by age: the room's **record retention**. Records older than it states become **eligible** to be removed by `rooms/records/prune`; nothing is removed until a holder of `admin` asks for a prune, and nothing a prune removes can be brought back.

**Not `retentionPolicy`, and not `retentionDays`.** Both names are taken in this family and mean other things. `retentionPolicy` (`RetentionPolicy`) is whether a room's *key chain* lets a member read epochs from before they joined, fixed at creation because key material either exists for an epoch or it does not. `retentionDays` (`rooms/create`) is how long a host keeps a whole room after it lapses unrenewed. This is a third question — how long the room keeps its *records* while it is live — and unlike the first it is a decision a room revisits, so it is changeable (`rooms/records/retention/set`). A name sharing either's would invite a reader to apply one's rules to the other.

**Age is the host's to measure, so age is `updatedAt`.** On the sealed tiers a host can read nothing of a record but its key, version, status, pinning and when it last changed, so a policy the host applies can only be stated in those terms. That is also why it cannot use a record's own `validUntil`, which is sealed: expiry is a reader's rule, retention a host's. A curation is a change, so it restarts a record's age — a retraction starts a tombstone's.

**Absent, or `{}`, means no record is ever eligible by age**, and that is the reading a host MUST apply whenever it cannot read a policy: removing data under a rule nobody stated is the failure this member exists to prevent. Every member can read the policy in force (`rooms/info`), so a record is never removed under a rule its readers could not have known.

ext.description: Ecosystem-defined extension members per SPEC.md §4.5.1. A host MUST NOT treat a member here as making more records eligible: a removal rule a member's reader cannot understand is one they were never told about.

recordDays.description: Days a record is kept after it last changed, whatever its standing. A record — `active`, `deprecated` or `retracted` — whose `updatedAt` is more than this long ago is eligible, **unless it is pinned**: pinning says what matters in the room, and a room that wants a pinned record gone unpins it first. Absent means records are never eligible by age.

tombstoneDays.description: Days a retracted record's tombstone is kept after its retraction. A tombstone whose `updatedAt` is more than this long ago is eligible. Tombstones exist so that a member syncing incrementally learns of a retraction (`rooms/records/curate`); this is how long a member may stay away and still learn of one that way rather than by rebuilding their copy of the room. Absent means tombstones are never eligible.

RecordRetention.title: RecordRetention

epoch.description: The epoch the room now stands at, as the host reports it. `1` for a room registered for the first time.

host.description: The host that accepted it, echoed so a caller recording where its room lives records what the recipient actually reached rather than what it asked for.

revocation.description: The room's revocation list as the recipient holds it, and what the host did with it. Present whenever the recipient holds a list for the room; absent only when it holds none. Anything but `inForce` means the host is serving the room without its withdrawals: it honours every credential the room has withdrawn until it accepts the list.

code.description: The host's error code. Present exactly when `status` is `refused`.

status.description: `inForce`: the host answered with this list's head. `pending`: the host did not answer, or answered with another head; the recipient goes on delivering it. `refused`: the host refused the list, with `code`; repeating the delivery changes nothing.

RetentionPolicy.$comment: Deliberately no JSON Schema `default`. A declared default is materialised by the generated bindings — the member becomes non-optional with a serde default — so an absent value would reappear as an explicit one on re-serialisation and break round-trip idempotence for every document written before this member existed. The meaning of absence is stated in prose, where a binding cannot act on it.
RetentionPolicy.description: Whether a room keeps its history readable across a membership change, fixed at creation and immutable thereafter — like `Visibility`, and for the same reason: the rungs of an epoch key chain either exist for an epoch or they do not, and no later change of mind can seal key material that was never sealed or unseal what was already severed. `chained`: each advance produces an `EpochLink`, so every member reads the room's whole retained history however long they have been in it — what a **library** wants, at the cost of post-compromise security for record content, since a compromised current key then reaches every retained epoch. `fromJoin`: no rungs are produced, so a member reads only from the epoch their group state is at — what a **stream** wants, and what a room under a strict forward-secrecy obligation wants, at the cost that a joining member finds an empty-looking room and nobody can reread a record once their group state has moved past the epoch it was sealed under. Absent means `chained`; see the prose on why the absent case is the readable one.
RetentionPolicy.title: RetentionPolicy

RevocationHead.description: Which `RevocationList` a party holds, without its entries: comparable between the room's key holder and a host, and between two hosts, without disclosing whom the room withdrew.

digest.description: SHA-256 multihash of the list's RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, `proof` included. Two parties holding one sequence with different digests have been given two lists the room signed at one sequence.

RevocationHead.title: RevocationHead

SignalDelay.description:
Whether a room's host waits a randomised interval before sending a `rooms/changed` signal: the room's **signal delay**.

`randomised` is the default and what a room without one has: the host waits a few seconds after the change that fires a watch, so that the signal's time does not mark one write exactly (`rooms/changed`, producer item 4). `none` is for a room where members expect to see a write as soon as it is made, such as a conversation: the host sends the signal as soon as the change that fires it is stored, with no wait of its own.

**A room's setting, not a member's.** The delay protects the room's writers as much as its watchers. A watcher whose signal is sent at once marks, to anyone who sees both the writer's request reach the host and the signal leave it, the moment of the write and that the two parties share the room. So one watcher cannot opt out for itself without giving away something about everyone who writes, and the setting is the room's: changed by a holder of `admin` (`rooms/signal-delay/set`) and served to every member (`rooms/info`).

**What `none` gives up.** Little in a busy room, where writes are frequent enough that their rhythm is visible anyway; most in a quiet one, where a single write and a single signal line up. A surface that offers the setting SHOULD say so.

Absent means `randomised`.
SignalDelay.title: SignalDelay

Visibility.description: How much of a room its host can see, fixed at creation and immutable thereafter. `open`: records are cleartext, searchable and fully audited. `attributed`: record content is sealed, and the host still learns which member acted. `private`: content is sealed and membership is presented in zero knowledge, so the host verifies that a member acted without learning which. Immutable because a downgrade cannot un-see cleartext and an upgrade would protect only what came after while presenting as though it protected everything.
Visibility.title: Visibility

host.description: The host to register with, as a DID. Named by the caller because a room has no host until this call succeeds, and because a room may be registered with more than one (a mirror serves reads while its primary takes writes).

ownerDid.description: The accountable party, and the issuer of the rooms/create document the recipient sends on its behalf: the recipient signs it with a key of this DID that it holds, never as itself. Absent means the caller — a registration is normally made by the owner it names. A recipient holding no key for it refuses with permissionDenied before contacting the host.

recordRetention.description: How long the room keeps its records, by age. Passed through to `rooms/create`, whose description governs; absent means no record is ever eligible by age.

retentionDays.description: How long the host is asked to hold the room after it lapses.

retentionPolicy.description: Whether the room keeps its history readable across a membership change. Immutable once set, so a caller that omits it is taking the host's default for the life of the room.

roomId.description: The room being registered. Its identity exists already — this asks a host to store it, not to name it.

signalDelay.description: Whether the host waits a randomised interval before sending the room's watch signals. Passed through to `rooms/create`, whose description governs; absent means `randomised`.

visibility.description: The tier to create the room at. Passed through to `rooms/create`, whose description of the choice governs.
